texts: mixed: every atom is true and the parse was judged compliant, but two parts of the wording sit in corners our instruction set does not cover - "Council touch" fuses into one kind symbol whose "council" half is deliberately not exposed, so nothing links this claim to the Council itself, and an object-position "no" has no defined route, so the word is consumed into the rule's falsity and leaves no trace. Rewriting costs you nothing on either count: "Replacement lanterns do not need a touch from the Council." - the negation then sits on the verb, where it is fully specified, and the Council becomes a referent your other Council sentences can join to.
